mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent competent corporate registrar in the foreign corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel mutually exclusive process only. If the issuing jurisdiction is a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention: notarize the document and obtain an Apostille from the competent national authority; do not add consular legalization. If the issuing jurisdiction is not an Apostille party: notarize the document, obtain Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization in the issuing country, then obtain consular legalization from the Republic of Korea embassy or consulate; do not obtain an Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or government authority in the foreign corporate shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel mutually exclusive process only. If the issuing jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state: notarize and Apostille only; never chain consular legalization. If the issuing jurisdiction is a non-member state: notarize, foreign ministry legalization, then Korean consular legalization only; never request an Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing Korean incorporation and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate shareholder's board of directors, certified by an authorized corporate officer or corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel mutually exclusive process only. For Apostille states: notarize the resolution and attach an Apostille from the competent authority; no consular stamp. For non-Apostille states: notarize the resolution, have it legalized by the issuing country's foreign ministry, and then legalized by the Korean embassy or consulate; no Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Memorandum of Association of foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate shareholder, via certified copy from the corporate registry or company secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel mutually exclusive process only. Apostille route: notarized copy plus Apostille only. Consular route: notarized copy plus issuing country foreign ministry legalization plus Korean consular legalization only. The two routes must never be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the foreign corporate shareholder's relationship bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing relationship bank of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Parallel mutually exclusive process only. Apostille route: bank signature notarized and an Apostille issued by the competent authority of the bank's country; stop there. Consular route: bank signature notarized, foreign ministry legalization, and Korean consular legalization; do not use an Apostille if the bank's country is not an Apostille member.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, officers, beneficial owners, counterparties, global distribution partners, and aviation-related vendors must be screened continuously against the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury sanctions list, and sanctions designations maintained by the Republic of Korea Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit, including designations under the Act on Prohibition of Financing for Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction. The protocol requires mandatory screening of domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons, adverse media review, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, 100% identification matching using passport or equivalent documents, direct and indirect ownership tracing through every intermediary layer, false-positive resolution by a qualified compliance officer, and enhanced due diligence for any PEP, sanctioned jurisdiction, shell-company structure, or nominee-shareholder pattern. All screening records, UBO evidence, risk ratings, and board-approval justifications must be retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Commercial Registration Name Clearance Portal operated by the Supreme Court of Korea through the Internet Registry Office and the Registration Division of the district court with jurisdiction over the prospective Chusik Hoesa registered office.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal company name (sangho) must be written in Hangul as a registered Korean name, and must contain a statutory element clearly identifying the entity as a Chusik Hoesa (stock company) in Korean transliteration. A foreign-language or Romanized name is permitted only as a non-legal auxiliary notation; it cannot replace the registered Hangul name. The four-tier naming convention requires: first, a distinctive Hangul trade name; second, the statutory stock-company suffix; third, no identity or confusing similarity with any previously registered name in the same registry district; and fourth, prior ministerial approval for any sensitive token. A purely Romanized name without an approved Hangul transliteration will be rejected by the registry.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Government of the Republic of Korea
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within one month from the date of written rejection notice, the applicant may file a written objection with the registry office or file an appeal against the registration disposition with the district court having jurisdiction under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act. The written objection must include the rejected name, the legal basis for clearance, evidence that no confusingly similar prior registration exists, and any ministerial pre-approval obtained for sensitive tokens. If the district court sustains the appeal, the registry must proceed with clearance. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may file a fresh name clearance application without prejudice, using a revised Hangul name and corrected supporting documents.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mail-receiving service is permissible only as an auxiliary correspondence address, not as the sole registered office of a Chusik Hoesa engaged in airline inflight catering. The National Tax Service, municipal licensing authorities, and regulated banks in South Korea require a verifiable physical place of business for food manufacturing and aviation catering because the entity must hold an airport catering or food business license, comply with food safety and aviation security requirements, maintain payroll and VAT records, support corporate account opening, allow site visits, and satisfy landlord and utility verification. A purely virtual office or mailbox address will be rejected by Korean banks for corporate account opening and will not satisfy the statutory license prerequisites.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: unrestricted physical access to cooking and plating areas, chilled and frozen storage, washable surfaces, pest control records, fire safety equipment, airport security-zone credentials, staff attendance and payroll records, accounting books and tax invoices, lease agreements, HACCP or equivalent food-safety certification, and the statutory license displayed at the registered premises. Quantified risk: greater than 80% probability of unannounced inspection by the National Tax Service or municipal food safety authority within the first 12 months of operation; approximately 15-25% probability of a municipal or registry site visit for newly registered corporations using shared or non-traditional office premises; and 100% mandatory inspection and audit of the bonded kitchen and ramp-delivery operations by the airport operator and customs authorities before initial inflight catering service begins.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fixed legal fee plus Korean Notary Fee Act schedule for corporate article notarization.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration tax and education surtax on incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local tax authority and district court registration fee collection office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registration Tax Act rate of 0.4% of paid-in capital plus 20% education surtax, assuming a Korean won equivalent of approximately USD 75,000 paid-in capital.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of Korea registry division through the district court
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court Registration Fee schedule at approximately 0.03-0.04% of stated capital.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Korean Notary Fee Act statutory tariff.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Korean translation of foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Public translator or certified translation office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-page public translator fee plus notarization of translator signature.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of the mandatory documentary bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent government authority in the issuing jurisdiction and, where applicable, the Republic of Korea embassy or consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official apostille or consular legalization fee schedule, excluding courier costs, selected strictly by the mutually exclusive Hague Apostille or consular route.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed-stage retainer for Stage 1 pre-incorporation compliance, not contingent and excluding government fees.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Issuing foreign bank and prospective Korean bank

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Articles 289 through 318 (formation, corporate governance and registration of a stock corporation), Article 317 (registration of incorporation), Article 390 (board of directors quorum and resolution), Articles 458 through 461 (legal reserves and capital maintenance); Food Sanitation Act and its Enforcement Decree for the licensed food manufacturing and processing operation; Environmental Impact Assessment Act for facilities requiring environmental assessment or registration; Fire Prevention, Safety Control and Civil Defense Framework Act for physical clearance.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, District Court Registry Office having jurisdiction over the registered office of the corporation, with online filing through the Korean Internet Registration Office (IRO) operated by the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company, culminating in the Certificate of Registration of Incorporation and certified corporate registry transcript.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is imposed on a Chusik Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. The Articles of Incorporation may lawfully provide for a zero or minimal stated capital. However, if any share subscription proceeds are collected, those funds must be deposited into a dedicated incorporation deposit or escrow account before registration, and the bank subscription certificate must be attached to the registration filing. After the court issues the Certificate of Registration, the block is lifted and funds are released for corporate use. There is no mandatory continuing blocked capital escrow account, but the statutory legal reserve rule in Commercial Act Article 458 applies as retained earnings accumulate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
BEFORE THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [CORPORATION NAME], A STOCK CORPORATION ORGANIZED PURSUANT TO THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA.
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS
1. Organization and Quorum. The Board of Directors of [CORPORATION NAME] (the Company) convened its first meeting on [DATE], at [PLACE], upon due notice to all incumbent directors. There are [NUMBER] directors, representing the entire board, and all directors are present either physically or by valid proxy, establishing a lawful quorum pursuant to Article 390 of the Commercial Act.
2. Adoption of Articles of Association. The Board reviewed and unanimously adopted the Articles of Association, including the corporate purpose, authorized shares, initial paid-in capital and governance provisions, and declared that the same are consistent with the registration instrument submitted to the competent district court.
3. Subscription and Issuance. The Board confirmed that all shares of common stock subscribed as of this date have been appropriately issued to the respective founding shareholders, that the statutory paid-in capital or lawful zero-capital position has been fully credited or documented, that the incorporation deposit block has been verified, and that no share issuance exceeds the limitations contained in the Articles of Association.
4. Registered Office. The Board resolved that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [ADDRESS], a lawful jurisdictional seat within South Korea, and directed the Representative Director to complete the registered office entry in the commercial registry and to notify all relevant licensing, taxing and environmental agencies.
5. Banking Authorizations. The Board resolved to open corporate operating, invoicing and settlement accounts at [BANK], in the name of the Company, under the Corporate Tax Identification Number assigned by the National Tax Service. The Representative Director, Financial Director or any single designated officer under a dual signature control matrix shall be authorized to give instructions, sign instruments, issue aviation payroll and supplier payment orders, and manage all settlement rails for wire and ACH transactions when accompanied by the required approval thresholds.
6. Appointment of Officers. The Board unanimously appointed the following officers: Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer [NAME], Financial Director [NAME], Corporate Secretary [NAME] and Statutory Auditor [NAME], each subject to the eligibility requirements of the Commercial Act, with authority and tenure beginning on [DATE] and continuing until otherwise terminated by shareholder action. The Board accepted all duties and responsibilities for the accuracy of corporate records and the timely filing of statutory reports.
7. Delegation and Execution. The Board authorized the Corporate Secretary to prepare and submit the incorporation registration, business registration, HACCP and MFDS license dossiers, environmental registration forms, civil defense fire safety applications and all ancillary documents. All prior acts performed on behalf of the Company before the effective time are hereby ratified, and this Resolution is effective immediately pending notarized registration, if required by any third-party authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search, Articles of Incorporation Drafting and Notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean Internet Registration Office (IRO) operated by the Supreme Court of Korea for name search; notarization before a Korean notary public located in the district court jurisdiction of the proposed registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a pre-application name search on the IRO to confirm that no identical or confusingly similar company name already exists under Article 254 of the Commercial Act. Then prepare the Articles of Incorporation in the official statutory language, specifying the exact corporate purpose: airline in-flight meal manufacturing, HACCP catering production, bonded warehouse operations, airport ramp delivery and ancillary aviation food logistics. The Articles must be executed by all promoters and then appear before a notary public, who certifies the execution and identity of the promoters. Include the initial share classes, par value, incorporation date, number of directors, statutory auditor and corporate seat. The notarized Articles must be attached to the registration file and will serve as the constitution of the company for all subsequent court, tax and licensing applications.
required_dossiers: Promoter identity and proof of legal capacity
Corporate name search result or name reservation confirmation
Draft Articles of Incorporation with all statutory items
Subscription agreement and share allocation schedule
Certified copy of passports or resident registration records for each promoter
Consent forms of prospective directors and statutory auditor
Notarization application and proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search or notarization is queried, the filer must submit a corrected name declaration and more precise distinguishing character within 5 business days through the IRO. If the notary declines due to document insufficiency, the promoter shall cure by re-executing the Articles, attaching apostilled identity documents and paying the applicable notarial correction fee, after which the examiner resumes processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Capital Subscription and Verification Bank Account Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any licensed domestic commercial bank under the Banking Act of South Korea; Financial Supervisory Service as the banking supervisory reference for resolving bank onboarding objections.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Promoters shall open a dedicated incorporation deposit account at a licensed domestic commercial bank using the pre-reserved corporate name, or through a bank name-reservation protocol if the final name has not yet been registered. Each founding shareholder remits the subscribed consideration to that account, and the bank issues a capital deposit certificate stating the subscriber, amount and settlement date. In a zero paid-in capital formation, the promoters must execute a notarized zero-subscription statement and obtain written confirmation from the bank that a permanent operating account can be opened immediately after the court issues the Certificate of Registration. The bank certificate and subscription ledger are mandatory for the commercial registration filing.
required_dossiers: IRO name reservation approval
Founder identity, passport or resident registration certificate
Subscription schedule and share ledger summary
Bank capital deposit certificate, or notarized zero-subscription statement
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal sample if required by bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the incorporation account due to name ambiguity or AML doubts, submit the IRO name-reservation certificate, beneficial ownership declaration and source-of-funds evidence, and escalate to the bank AML compliance officer. In the alternative, select another licensed bank and repeat the same simplified KYC pack; the banker shall not request a capital minimum because no statutory minimum applies to a Chusik Hoesa.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing Commercial Registration with the District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office; online submission through the Korean Internet Registration Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company after notarization and paid-in capital evidence are complete. The application must list the corporate name, corporate purpose, registered office, number of directors, statutory auditor and representative officer. The filer must pay the court registration fee and local education tax, obtain the payment receipt and submit the electronic or paper dossier. The registry examiner checks conformity of the Articles, the legitimacy of officer consents, the capital subscription certificate, and the registered office proof. If all conditions are satisfied, the court issues the Certificate of Registration of Incorporation and a certified corporate registry transcript. The legal representative must then file a specimen signature and corporate seal with the court if required under local practice.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Registration of Incorporation
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank capital deposit certificate or zero-subscription statement
Consent and eligibility declarations from each director and auditor
Identity documents of the legal representative
Registration tax and education tax payment receipts
Lease agreement or ownership evidence for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry examiner issues a supplementary order, the applicant must cure the indicated defects within 5 business days by uploading corrected documents to the IRO. If the corporate name conflicts with a prior similar name, the directors must amend the Articles and re-notarize. If the registered office proof is insufficient, submit a revised lease agreement and floor plan. Once the supplementary order is satisfied, the court continues review without a new application fee, apart from copy or transcript fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Organization, Business Registration and Permanent Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the competent District Tax Office and Hometax online system; the registered commercial bank for account activation; Financial Supervisory Service for banking standard oversight.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after receiving the Certificate of Registration, the Board must lawfully meet to adopt corporate governance minutes covering share certificates, accounting period, audit procedures, fiscal year and signing rules. The legal representative must file a Business Registration Certificate application through the National Tax Service Hometax portal within 20 days from the start of operations, declaring the detailed business category as ISIC 5621 food manufacturing and aviation catering, including the registered workplace, representative, VAT type and banking details. The corporate bank account is then activated using the registration certificate, corporate seal, notarized board resolution and officer identity documents. The company must also enroll in mandatory social insurance with the legal employers and workers under national pension, health insurance, employment and industrial accident insurance rules.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Incorporation
Certificate of corporate seal
Articles of Incorporation and first board resolution minutes
Business Registration Certificate application form
Identity certificates of legal representative and officers
Lease agreement for the registered office
Bank account opening application and AML declarations
Workplace facility layout plan and kitchen equipment summary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service queries the business classification, submit an ISIC/NAICS bridging letter and the MFDS food manufacturing report as evidence of the active catering operation. If a lease defect is identified, amend the registered office by filing a change-of-registered-office application with the district court before reapplying. If the bank imposes enhanced due diligence, provide the beneficial ownership chain, catering contracts and HACCP licensing timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Safety, Industrial and Environmental Licensing and Civil Defense Fire Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) through the local office having jurisdiction over the catering kitchen; Ministry of Environment and the Korea Environment Corporation for environmental permitting and inspection; local Fire Department under the National Fire Agency for civil defense and fire safety clearance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a Food Manufacturing and Processing Business Report with the local MFDS office, including the HACCP plan for airline in-flight meal production, facility floor plan, machinery list, potable water supply, waste management plan and sanitation standard operating procedures. Register the pollution control installation with the local environmental agency for the cooking operation, disclosing exhaust stack parameters, grease trap capacity, wastewater flow, permitted discharge routes and waste disposal contracts. Submit a building fire safety and civil defense clearance application to the local fire department, covering fire alarms, kitchen hood suppression, emergency exits, fire extinguisher placement, chemical storage and evacuation planning. After all approvals are granted, secure the operating licenses and place the recurring inspection dates on the corporate compliance calendar. If the catering facility must enter the airside ramp area, the airport operator shall be updated with the licenses and the company added as an approved access party under the airport security program.
required_dossiers: Food Manufacturing and Processing Business Report application
Facility layout plan and equipment specifications
HACCP plan and food safety management certification
Wastewater discharge and grease trap design report
Air emission control system specifications
Waste disposal contracts and waste manifest templates
Fire safety plan and emergency evacuation map
Building inspection certificate
Airport ramp access entitling contract, only if airside delivery is required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MFDS identifies deficiencies during the facility inspection, implement the corrective action plan within 20 days and request reinspection. If the environmental authority sets stricter conditions, submit a remediation plan with laboratory-measured pollutant loads and install additional grease, VOC or wastewater treatment units. If the fire department withholds the civil defense certificate, immediately correct the life-safety defect, obtain a structural fire engineer review and apply for urgent reinspection; the plant may not begin commercial production until full clearance is issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), local Sigu-Gun health and environmental licensing office, Ministry of Environment (MOE) for environmental assessment and the local Fire Department under the National Fire Agency for civil defense and fire safety clearance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Manufacturing and Processing Business Report and Registration Certificate, together with HACCP Plan Approval for Airline In-Flight Catering; additional Fire Safety Completion Inspection Certificate and Civil Defense Preparedness Clearance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOE) – Environmental Impact Assessment Division and Korea Environment Corporation for technical review and pollution control inspection.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Three-tier environmental assessment ladder: Tier 3, Environmental Registration, applies to a catering kitchen with site floor area below 1,000 square meters and wastewater discharge below 200 cubic meters per day; Tier 2, Small-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment, is required when floor area equals or exceeds 1,000 square meters or wastewater discharge equals or exceeds 200 cubic meters per day; Tier 1, Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report, is required if the facility is located in an ecological or water-source protection zone, or has production capacity exceeding 10,000 meals per day, or generates high-load organic wastewater in excess of 2,000 kilograms of COD per day.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to municipal sewer from the catering kitchen must meet the following quantitative compliance thresholds: pH 5.8 to 8.6, BOD not exceeding 30 mg/L, COD not exceeding 40 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L, total nitrogen not exceeding 60 mg/L, total phosphorus not exceeding 8 mg/L, and oil and grease not exceeding 5 mg/L. If wastewater is discharged directly to a water body, BOD and suspended solids must not exceed 10 mg/L. Cooking exhaust must pass through grease capture equipment and a high-efficiency electrostatic filter with stack total volatile organic compounds not exceeding 200 ppm. Odors are controlled under the Malodor Prevention Act with a boundary dilution threshold of not less than 500. Hazardous waste, used cooking oil and food waste must be tracked by waste manifest and transported to licensed disposal, feed conversion or energy recovery facilities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Completion Inspection Certificate issued by the local Fire Department for the building, including automatic fire detection, sprinkler or suppression systems, kitchen hood fire suppression, emergency lighting, exit signage and evacuation routes. Civil Defense Preparedness Clearance requires the submission of a protective action and evacuation plan, participation in municipal civil defense communication protocols and structural load classification for the building. Occupational safety and health clearance is issued through the Ministry of Employment and Labor workplace risk assessment, covering machine guarding, food processing blade safety, hot oil and steam handling, sanitation disease prevention, personal protective equipment, work hours and welfare facility compliance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea, operating through the HomeTax electronic portal (hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity establishing a Chusik Hoesa, the entity must file an application for Business Registration (사업자등록신청) with the NTS via HomeTax or the local tax office within 20 days of business commencement. The representative director or local tax representative must submit the corporate registration certificate, articles of incorporation, certificate of foreign investment registration under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (if applicable), and documentation evidencing the physical place of business. Upon successful review, the NTS assigns a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which serves as the VAT, corporate tax, and local tax identifier. Foreign entities without a domestic place of business must appoint a tax representative for filing and payment obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Korean tax law. A Chusik Hoesa is automatically taxed as a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act. The only relevant elective mechanism is the consolidated corporate taxation regime for wholly-owned subsidiaries under Article 12 of the Corporate Tax Act, available for groups meeting statutory shareholding and filing requirements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold; every business operator supplying goods or services in the course of a business is mandatorily required to register for VAT with the NTS within 20 days of business commencement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses issuing tax invoices for B2B supplies must issue mandatory electronic tax invoices (전자세금계산서) through the NTS HomeTax system within one day after the invoice issuance date. There is no real-time clearance or fiscal stamping requirement, but the e-invoice data is transmitted digitally to the NTS through the standard HomeTax API or portal interface. Failure to issue an e-invoice or late transmission subjects the supplier to an additional tax penalty of 1% of the invoice value. Additionally, cashier receipts are required for consumer transactions as fraud prevention.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean VAT Act and its Enforcement Decree, zero-rating applies to exported goods and certain internationally-connected services. For in-flight catering supplies to airlines, zero-rating is available when the goods are loaded onto an aircraft operating an international route, evidencing that the meals are exported from Korea for consumption outside Korean territorial waters. The service is also zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident airline and the benefit is consumed entirely outside South Korea, provided the proceeds are received in foreign currency and repatriated. The taxpayer must retain documentary proof of the export transaction and foreign exchange receipt.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (수출신고필증 / Export Declaration Confirmation)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill covering the international flight and consignment
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or foreign exchange bank receipt showing receipt of the export proceeds in an approved foreign currency
Electronic tax invoice (zero-rated) issued to the airline customer
Sales contract or purchase order from the foreign airline specifying international route and catering service
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly audit export zero-rating claims. If the export declaration, transportation documents, sales contract, or foreign exchange repatriation records are missing, incomplete, or falsified, the claimed zero-rate is retroactively reversed and VAT at 10% is clawed back with statutory interest. False claims constitute unlawful tax evasion, subject to an additional penalty up to 40% of the evaded tax amount, criminal fines up to twice the amount of tax evaded, and imprisonment for up to two years, in accordance with the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), with foreign exchange policy authority exercised jointly by the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) reporting framework
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South Korean won is fully convertible for current account transactions, including ordinary trade settlement, service fees, and repatriation of legally declared dividends, subject to documentary verification by an authorized domestic foreign exchange bank. Capital account transactions are not freely convertible; they require prior declaration, notification, or reporting to the Bank of Korea through a domestic foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Inward foreign direct investment and outward investment remittances must be filed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and the Foreign Exchange Information System, and the financing bank must validate the purpose code and underlying contract. There is no general obligation to surrender export proceeds to the Bank of Korea, but all foreign currency receipts must be received through a domestic authorized foreign exchange bank and reported. Profit remittances by a Chusik Hoesa are permitted once audited financial statements, tax clearance certificates, and board approval of dividends are presented, and the remittance must be processed through a domestic bank where the corporate account is maintained. For a foreign-invested inflight catering company, the practical hurdle is not convertibility itself but the KYC and capital verification evidence required for the foreign exchange bank to approve each remittance. Payment for imported food ingredients, aviation galley equipment, and licensing royalties must be supported by relevant trade documentation and declared under the applicable FEIS transaction code. Capital account liberalization is extensive, yet Korea retains administrative screening and anti-money laundering scrutiny over unusual or large cross-border flows, particularly where the beneficial owner is a non-resident corporation or where the intended use deviates from the declared corporate purpose.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For inflight catering supplies classified as exports from Korea under the Customs Act, export proceeds must be collected through an authorized foreign exchange bank within one year from the date of export declaration. There is no statutory mandatory surrender ratio to the Bank of Korea; however, the exporting Chusik Hoesa must settle the foreign currency receipt into its domestic KRW account or maintain it in a foreign currency account at the same domestic bank, and the receipt must be reported to the Foreign Exchange Information System. Any extension beyond the one-year collection period requires prior approval from the Ministry of Economy and Finance, with documentary support such as airline purchase orders, delivery certificates, and evidence of an unavoidable delay in settlement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs are not viable as the primary banking or clearing rail for a Korean Chusik Hoesa. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act, a corporate entity operating in Korea must maintain its operational and foreign exchange settlement accounts with an authorized domestic financial institution. Offshore EMI platforms such as global digital payment providers do not possess a Korean banking licence and cannot provide a compliant KRW clearing account, foreign exchange reporting, or capital verification services acceptable to the Bank of Korea. A fintech EMI may be used only as a supplementary ancillary tool for travel expenses or low-value procurement, but it cannot replace the domestic tier-one commercial bank relationship, cannot accept foreign direct investment capital, and is legally barred from servicing the company as its clearing bank.

stage_4.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors of a newly formed Chusik Hoesa with non-resident ownership must appear physically in-branch at a tier-one domestic commercial bank in Korea for corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening and remote video onboarding are not permitted as the sole authentication method for initial account activation of a risk-rated corporate entity. After the statutory director completes the physical in-branch interview, additional authorised signatories may be subjected to a vetted video interview or consular verification procedure on a case-by-case basis at the bank compliance committee's discretion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Tax Return and Financial Statement Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 of the following year for a December 31 fiscal year-end; within three months after fiscal year-end for other fiscal year closes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underpayment penalty of 20 percent of the deficient tax, daily delinquency interest of 0.022 percent on unpaid amounts, administrative collection seizure, and potential criminal liability for willful non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' General Meeting and Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Statutory corporate records maintained at the head office; no government authority filing is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; by March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the meeting or preserve minutes may be subject to administrative fines not exceeding KRW 5 million; failure to record resolutions may render them ineffective

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) via Open DART, submitted by the external auditor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the statutory period after the close of the fiscal year, ordinarily by end of April for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to undergo a mandatory external audit constitutes a violation of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and may result in administrative fines, auditor designation orders, and nullification of audited financial statements for certain corporate purposes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surcharge and Education Tax Annual Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal tax office (Si/Gun/Gu) through the local e-tax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the corporate tax return, March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 10 percent on unpaid local surcharge, daily delinquency interest of 0.022 percent, and coercive collection against corporate assets

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent external audit applies when the company's total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion at the preceding fiscal year-end; lower thresholds or special rules may apply for public-interest entities and certain financial or licensed businesses. A privately held Chusik Hoesa below the threshold is not statutorily required to appoint an external auditor unless shareholders so resolve.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for companies subject to external audit and companies required to use K-IFRS; Korean GAAP for smaller non-public companies. Financial statements must be prepared in Korean won in accordance with the Korean Commercial Act and the External Audit Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO confirmation filing exists under Korean corporate law. Shareholder changes are reflected in the register of members when share transfer is presented for registration. For AML purposes, financial institutions must identify and verify beneficial owners through customer due diligence, and the company must maintain accurate internal shareholder and beneficial ownership records. The company is not required to file an annual UBO declaration with a corporate registry in Korea.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - 600 per annum for standard registered office or corporate secretarial agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 12,000 for a certified external audit when the statutory threshold is met; USD 1,500 - 3,000 for a unqualified accountant-reviewed compilation when audit is not mandatory

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax (CIT) on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; the effective combined rate with local income tax (10% surtax on CIT) is 26.4%. Progressive national rates apply: 9% up to KRW 200 million; 19% between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion; 21% between KRW 20 billion and KRW 300 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays and preferential deductions primarily include: (i) R&D expenses tax credit (up to 15-25% depending on company size) under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act (RST); (ii) facility investment tax credit (1-3% for equipment); (iii) job creation and employment preservation credit; (iv) foreign-invested high-technology or airport-supporting logistics services under Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) may access 50% exemption from CIT for 5 years and 50% reduction for the following 2 years; (v) SME tax reduction and payroll increase credits under RST; (vi) investment in environmental and safety facilities carries additional deductions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Bubinse Gyesanseo) Form No. 1 or Form No. 3 for foreign-invested corporations; mandatory electronic filing through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return with semi-annual interim prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final income tax return must be filed within 3 months from the end of the fiscal year. For a fiscal year ending December 31, the due date is March 31 of the following year. Interim prepayments (for the first 6 months) are due within 2 months after the end of the first half of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered company name, business registration number, foreign investment registration number, tax office jurisdiction, and fiscal year period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name of the Korean Chusik Hoesa as registered with the Korean Commercial Registry. Attach the business registration certificate and the foreign investment registration certificate (if applicable). A foreign-controlled entity must also provide the ultimate parent legal entity name and jurisdiction.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge) on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders (unless reduced under an applicable tax treaty).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke double tax treaty (DTA) relief, the Korean payor must: (i) obtain from the non-resident shareholder a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority; (ii) submit the standard Korean withholding tax treaty benefit application form (Tax Treaty Exemption or Reduction Claim for Non-Resident) to the local tax office before payment, or alternatively claim a refund within 5 years through the NTS Entity Tax Refund procedure; (iii) execute the beneficial ownership declaration with supporting documentation, including ownership chain, business substance, and board resolutions proving the non-resident is not a conduit entity. The DTA rate for dividends is typically 10-15%, and 0% in some treaties for substantial shareholding (25% or more).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 22% (20% national tax plus 2% local surtax). Under most Korean DTAs: interest is commonly reduced to 10-15%; royalties from industrial and intellectual property are usually reduced to 10-15% but may be as high as 20% for certain license arrangements. Any reduction requires submission of TRC and treaty claim form to the NTS before the remittance; otherwise tax must be withheld in full and refund claimed afterward.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory local file and master file are required when cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion per fiscal year. Additionally, a master file is compulsory if the Korean enterprise is part of a multinational group with consolidated revenue at or above KRW 100 billion. Country-by-Country Reporting (CbCR) applies where group consolidated revenue is at or above KRW 1 trillion, and reporting must be lodged electronically in accordance with the International Tax Adjustment Act.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea applies a statutory substance-over-form doctrine under the Corporate Tax Act (Article 9-1) and the Framework Act on National Taxes (Article 17). Tax treaty benefits are denied where a non-resident or a foreign entity lacks beneficial ownership or substantive business activity. For an airline in-flight catering kitchen, the Korean tax authorities (NTS) will expect: an active operational license from the Civil Aviation Authority, physical kitchen and refrigerated storage premises, a team of production and logistics employees, actual delivery contracts with airlines, independent management decision-making, and distributive pools. A mere pass-through invoicing arrangement or EBITDA-stripping corporate shell will trigger anti-avoidance re-characterization and forfeiture of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Income Tax Evasion (Intentional Underreporting / False Evidence)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of in-flight meal sales, fabrication of purchase invoices for food ingredients, or creation of fictitious airline contracts to reduce reported taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, criminal penalty: imprisonment up to 5 years (extended to 7 years in aggravated cases) and a fine not exceeding five times the evaded tax. Additionally, the NTS assesses underreported tax penalties of 20% (40% if involving false audited statements) plus daily late-payment surcharges of 0.022% on any overdue tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who ordered or knowingly benefited from the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax. Several liability also arises under the secondary tax collection rules. Travel bans (prohibition of departure from Korea) are routinely imposed during tax investigations. In egregious cases, the responsible CEO and CFO face personal criminal imprisonment, civil restitution, and lifetime disqualification from corporate directorship.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Empty Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance in In-flight Catering Operation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a Korean Chusik Hoesa that merely invoices margins to foreign airline affiliates without possessing own kitchen, employees, inventory risk, or procurement autonomy; marketing or repatriating profits to the foreign parent while actual catering services are rendered from a foreign jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NTS will re-characterize the arrangement under substance-over-form principles, deny treaty benefits, subject the full margin to Korean CIT at 24% plus local tax, and exact a 20% deficiency penalty. Civil administrative penalties also include asset freezing. The Foreign Exchange Transaction Act may impose fines for unregistered foreign transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may trigger piercing of the corporate veil if capital is clearly inadequate and the shell is used for fraud. The NTS can hold directors personally liable for the entire tax debt and penalties under Article 14-2 of the Basic Law on Local Taxes (secondary tax liability). Travel restrictions and a ban on leaving Korea are automatic during criminal investigations for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-Pricing Manipulation / Failure to Maintain TP Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying inflated food procurement prices to foreign group entities, charging below-arm's-length margins to overseas airline customers, or failing to prepare mandatory local/master file despite cross-border related-party transactions exceeding KRW 5 billion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: NTS assesses the arm's-length price (KPGA) and recalculates the Korean entity's taxable income upward; a penalty of 20% of the additional attributable tax applies. Additionally, non-documentation of TP arrangements carries a penalty of up to KRW 100 million under the International Tax Adjustment Act. Interest on the deficiency accrues at 0.022% per day.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where directors are complicit in documenting a fabricated transfer-pricing policy, they are subject to secondary liability for the adjusted tax and penalties. The NTS may seek delegation of criminal referral for document forgery, which carries up to 5 years' imprisonment. Foreign travel bans remain active while criminal matters are pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to report inbound capital injection from the foreign parent under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; executing outbound profit remittances without documentation of underlying in-flight catering contracts; mixing cash proceeds from duty-free airport sales into the corporate bank account without Fl Advocacy report.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Korea's Financial Transactions Reports Act (FTRA), unregistered foreign exchange transactions are punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 50 million. Failure to file cash transaction reports over KRW 10 million triggers an administrative fine of up to KRW 20 million. The Financial Services Commission (FSC) can also suspend the corporate's currency conversion activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are criminally liable for laundering criminal proceeds exposed in tax investigations; sanctions merge with tax evasion charges. The Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission imposes travel bans and financial account freezing. Directors can be sentenced to up to 3 years for money laundering and deprivation of the right to operate a regulated business.
